title: Correctness of the Junta Node Continuation
statement: Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, let $P\subseteq[n]$, and fix a sign assignment $z:P\to\{\pm1\}$. Let $\delta\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy $0<\delta\le 1/2$, and let the sampled input be either absent or a batch of the prescribed size whose examples agree with $z$ on $P$. If this sampled input is not bad for the node procedure, then the probability that the continuation returns a bad node decision is at most zero.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
the sampled input is absent or is a batch of the prescribed size matched to $z$
the sampled input is not bad for the node procedure
